In GSE, this maps directly to dynamic bankroll sizing where stakes are adjusted according to estimated edge and variance. The Brier Score serves as a calibration metric for evaluating how well predicted probabilities match actual outcomes, forming a key component of GSI's probabilistic inference engine. Monte Carlo simulations allow for stress-testing these models under various stochastic regimes, enabling GSE to compute risk-adjusted expectations and validate stake sizes against simulated trajectories. These primitives form a closed-loop system where calibrated forecasts drive optimal staking, which is then validated through simulation-based risk assessment.
